survived.title: set_custom_segments is a REPLACE-ALL write that cannot name its target layout — it lands on whatever layout is active at call time, destroying another layout's authored geometry
survived.what_code_does: _handle_set_custom_segments takes only (vacuum_entity_id, map_id, segments[, backdrop_width/height]) — SET_CUSTOM_SEGMENTS_SCHEMA (line 378-397) and services.yaml both have NO layout_id field. The target is resolved server-side from global state at line 1667 (`layout = _ensure_default_layout(map_bucket)` -> `_active_custom_layout` -> `map_bucket['active_custom_layout_id']`), then line 1710 does `layout['custom_segments'] = {...}` — a full replace of that layout's authored polygons with no merge, no confirmation, no undo, and no prior-value capture. The card's compose-save (src/bindings/map.js:1382-1421) then loops `set_segment_room_link(mapId, seg.id, ...)` once per segment — also layout-less, also resolved through _resolve_active_scope at call time. Contrast the sibling writer _handle_upload_map_image (line 849-875), which REQUIRES layout_id and returns {'saved': false, 'reason': 'layout_not_found'} if it does not resolve: the identity guard exists in this file, but only on the non-destructive path.
survived.reproduction: Two card instances on the same map (wall tablet + phone — normal HA usage). (1) Tablet is in custom mode on layout 'Upstairs' (active), user composes 6 shapes. (2) Phone user taps the layout picker for 'Downstairs' -> set_active_custom_layout -> map_bucket['active_custom_layout_id'] = downstairs_id. (3) Tablet taps Save. set_custom_segments resolves the active layout = Downstairs and overwrites Downstairs' custom_segments with the 6 Upstairs shapes; the following set_segment_room_link loop writes Upstairs' room links into Downstairs' links dict (and its 1:1 rule at line 1843-1846 POPS Downstairs' own links for each colliding room). Result: 'Upstairs' unchanged (the user believes it saved), 'Downstairs' authored geometry gone. Single-client variant: the Save button is disabled while busy (src/renderers/map.js:1527) but the layout-picker buttons are NOT — tapping another layout during the multi-await save (set_custom_segments, then N awaited set_segment_room_link calls, each awaiting manager.async_save()) splits one save across two layouts. That is a gap ACROSS awaits inside a single HA event loop, not an interleaving fantasy.
survived.user_impact: Silent, unrecoverable loss of hand-authored map geometry plus its room links. The layout the user was editing is left untouched and the one they were not looking at is destroyed; the service returns {'saved': True, 'segment_count': N} either way, so nothing surfaces. Requires either two clients or an in-flight layout switch — the single-client, single-tab path is fine.
survived.guards_checked: _ensure_default_layout (line 1596) — guarantees SOME layout exists, never that it is the intended one; the card's _composeLoadedFor/_composeKey (src/state/map.js:1418) — client-side only, keyed on the LAST fetched active_custom_layout_id, never re-validated before saving and never sent to the server; _handle_upload_map_image's layout_not_found validation — present, but only on the upload path; manager.async_save() — persists, no optimistic-concurrency token or version check anywhere in the bucket; the `if not res?.saved` check in the card binding — only catches no_custom_backdrop, not wrong-target.
survived.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.2 + §10.4 ('rebuilds the **active layout's** custom_segments store from scratch each call (replace-all)') and docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'The active-scope seam' ('set_custom_segments targets the active layout'). The docs calmly DESCRIBE active-layout targeting; neither states that the client is unable to name the layout, and neither reconciles it with §10.3, which requires layout_id on the far less destructive upload path. services.yaml:2449-2457 is additionally stale — it says the call 'Rebuilds the map's custom segment set' (no mention of layouts at all) and 'Requires a custom backdrop image', which the live-dims path at line 1673-1682 has superseded.
survived.brands_affected: Both (Eufy + Roborock) — custom layouts are brand-independent map-bucket state.

survived.title: In custom mode with no resolvable layout, _resolve_active_scope hands writers THROWAWAY dicts — set_companion_anchor / set_segment_room_link mutate a garbage-collected object and report saved: True
survived.what_code_does: _resolve_active_scope's no-layout branch (lines 1550-1554) returns freshly-constructed `{}` literals for segments_store/links/anchors. They are not reachable from manager.data. _handle_set_companion_anchor (line 1890) binds `anchors = _resolve_active_scope(map_bucket)['anchors']`, writes `anchors[room_id] = {...}`, calls `await manager.async_save()` (which serialises manager.data — the anchor is not in it), and returns `{'saved': True, 'action': 'set', 'companion_anchors': {<the anchor>}}`. _handle_set_segment_room_link (line 1834) does the same for links. The third writer through the same seam, _handle_set_custom_segments, DOES call _ensure_default_layout first (line 1667) — the guard exists and was wired into one of the three siblings.
survived.reproduction: Reachable from the shipped card with no scripting. (1) A map with zero custom layouts. (2) User taps the Custom toggle: src/bindings/map.js:1228 -> set_segmentation_mode(mode='custom'). _handle_set_segmentation_mode line 1342-1345 soft-selects a layout only `if layouts:` — with `custom_layouts == {}` the branch is skipped, so the bucket is left at segmentation_mode='custom', active_custom_layout_id=None. (3) get_map_segments now serves segments=[] and companion_anchors={}. (4) The vacuum is docked, so the renderer falls through `if (!targetSeg) return this._mapAnimalDeviceFallback(...)` (src/renderers/map.js:1008) and draws the mascot with anchorKey='dock' — draggable. (5) User drags the mascot to park it. src/bindings/map.js:1944 optimistically updates local state and fires set_companion_anchor(mapId, 'dock', x, y), ignoring the response. Server writes into the throwaway dict, saves nothing, answers saved: True.
survived.user_impact: The mascot visibly stays where the user parked it for the rest of the session (the card never refetches after an anchor write) and silently snaps back on the next page load — repeatedly, with no error and no way for the user to tell the write failed. The same hole applies to set_segment_room_link for any script/automation caller. This is a result-returning API whose failure is not merely discarded but actively reported as success.
survived.guards_checked: _ensure_default_layout (line 1596) — the fix, wired into set_custom_segments only, absent from both other writers; _handle_set_segmentation_mode's soft-select (line 1342-1345) — gated on `if layouts:`, so it does not cover the zero-layout case that creates the state; _handle_delete_custom_layout's reassign-or-flip-to-cv (line 2422-2432) — covers deleting the last layout but not a map that never had one; _migrate_custom_layouts — seeds custom_layouts={} + active=None and returns, which is exactly the vulnerable state; the card's `if (!res?.saved)` check exists on compose-save but not on the anchor/link calls.
survived.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.2 states 'When no layout resolves, empty **read-only** stores are returned' — the author knew these dicts were not writable, yet two of the three writers that consume the seam mutate them and report success. docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'AnchorRecord' documents the dock anchor as persisted per-scope. Code/doc divergence either way: the doc says read-only, the code lets writers write.
survived.brands_affected: Both (Eufy + Roborock). The card path additionally needs a live map source present (mss.present) for the dock-mascot fallback, which is the normal Eufy fork configuration.

survived.title: _backfill_saved_zone_area fails OPEN on an indeterminate active map and permanently persists area_m2 / room_number computed from the WRONG map's raster — the poisoned value never self-heals
survived.what_code_does: Line 1449: `if not (active_map_id is None or str(active_map_id) == str(map_id)): return False` — i.e. an indeterminate active map PROCEEDS ('Indeterminate active map -> attempt'). It then calls `manager.async_get_map_data_dict(vacuum_entity_id=...)`, which returns the fork's currently-cached map_data for whatever map is loaded, with no map-identity field to cross-check against map_id. The derived area_m2 / room_number are written onto the zone (lines 1466-1469) and the caller persists them (line 1276-1279). Crucially, the `pending` filter is `z.get('area_m2') is None` (line 1434-1437), so once a wrong value is written the zone leaves the pending set FOREVER — there is no re-validation when the correct map later becomes active. get_active_map_id returns None on a blank/unavailable/unknown active-map entity and during the boot window (rooms/room_discovery.py:69-84), so 'indeterminate' is a routine transient state, not an exotic one.
survived.reproduction: Multi-floor Eufy household. Zone 'Under the dining table' was drawn on map B while map A was loaded, so create's identical guard left area_m2=None (this is precisely the population the backfill exists to repair). HA restarts (or the vacuum drops to unavailable) -> the active-map entity is blank -> get_active_map_id returns None. The user opens the card on map B; get_map_segments -> _backfill_saved_zone_area -> guard passes (active_map_id is None) -> async_get_map_data_dict returns map A's raster. Arithmetic, using zone_membership's own formula (area = Δnx*Δny*width*height*res²/10000): zone bbox Δnx=Δny=0.10. Map A width=800 height=600 res=5 -> 0.10*800*5 = 400 cm by 0.10*600*5 = 300 cm -> 12.0 m². Map B (the zone's real map) width=400 height=300 res=5 -> 200 cm by 150 cm -> 3.0 m². The zone is stamped 12.0 m² — 4x too large — plus a room_number taken from map A's room-id raster (Eufy room ids 1-11 are per-map, so 'room 3' on A is a different physical room from 'room 3' on B). manager.async_save() persists it, and because area_m2 is now non-None the zone is never re-examined.
survived.user_impact: Permanently wrong zone size shown in the card, a zone filed under the wrong room in the browse list (grouped by room_number per docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md), and a wrong area feeding the learning/duration-estimate path — which this function's own docstring claims it exists to make reliable. Irreversible from the UI: nothing recomputes area_m2 once set, so the only repair is editing .storage by hand. The single-map household is unaffected (the loaded map IS the zone's map); it needs 2+ maps plus a blank active-map entity at read time.
survived.guards_checked: The active-map guard at line 1449 itself — present, but the `active_map_id is None` arm inverts it; get_active_map_id's own sentinel handling (rooms/room_discovery.py:69) — it returns None precisely when it cannot tell, which is the arm that fails open; the create-time guard at line 2503 — identical shape, same fail-open, so the two paths agree on the wrong answer rather than one rescuing the other; map_data carries no map-id field to cross-check, and async_get_map_data_dict (map_source_coordinator.py:665) takes only vacuum_entity_id, so the callee cannot help; zone_membership is defensive but has no way to know which map it was handed; there is no re-heal path because `pending` keys on area_m2 being None.
survived.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §4 + lines 57-59 (area_m2 'computed from map dims at author time (display + validation)', room_number 'auto-set at author by >=90% dominance'); map_source.zone_membership's own docstring ('Roborock has no per-pixel raster... area_m2 needs the Eufy width/height/resolution dims'); docs/dev/10-learning-system.md:632 (zone area feeds the estimate). No doc states or defends 'when the active map is unknown, size the zone against whatever raster is loaded' — the inline comment asserts the guard 'mirrors create's guard', which is true but is a claim about consistency, not about correctness.
survived.brands_affected: Eufy only — on Roborock async_get_map_data_dict returns None early (map_source_coordinator.py:683), so nothing is written.

survived.title: _backfill_saved_zone_area overwrites a user's explicit 'Unassigned' filing — room_number=None means both 'never computed' and 'user chose Unassigned', and the read path cannot tell them apart
survived.what_code_does: Line 1467-1468: `if zone.get('room_number') is None and membership.get('room_number') is not None: zone['room_number'] = membership.get('room_number')`. The sentinel for 'not yet computed' is the same value the user's own override writes: _handle_set_saved_zone_room (line 2573) sets `zone['room_number'] = room_number` where SET_SAVED_ZONE_ROOM_SCHEMA (line 476-484) makes null an explicit, documented choice meaning Unassigned. There is no `filed_by`/`room_number_source` flag, no separate 'computed' key, and no boolean to distinguish the two states — classic absent-is-not-a-value conflation.
survived.reproduction: (1) Zone created while a different map was loaded, or with no map data available -> area_m2=None, room_number=None. (2) User opens the zone panel and files it under 'Kitchen' (set_saved_zone_room room_number=5). area_m2 is still None, so the zone stays in `pending`. (3) User changes their mind and picks Unassigned (set_saved_zone_room room_number=null) -> room_number=None, persisted, exactly as documented. (4) The zone's map later becomes active and the user opens the card. _backfill_saved_zone_area sees area_m2 is None -> computes membership -> sets area_m2 AND, because room_number is None, re-files the zone under the >=90%-dominant room. The user's deliberate Unassigned is gone, on a READ, with no service call from them.
survived.user_impact: A saved zone silently jumps out of the Unassigned section into a room section the user explicitly moved it out of. Filing only — docs are explicit that room_number never affects dispatch, so no wrong physical clean. Narrow: only bites zones that reached the user-editing stage while still unsized (i.e. authored off-active-map or with no map data). Once a zone has an area_m2 it is out of `pending` and immune.
survived.guards_checked: The `zone.get('room_number') is None` test at line 1467 — it IS the bug, not a guard; the `pending` filter (line 1434) — narrows the population but does not exclude user-edited zones, because a user can file/unfile a zone whose area_m2 is still None; _handle_set_saved_zone_room (line 2557-2576) — writes room_number and bumps updated_at but records no provenance the backfill could consult; nothing in _create_saved_zone (line 1396-1417) distinguishes a computed None from a chosen None either.
survived.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md lines 57-59 ('room_number ... auto-set at author by >=90% dominance, else None ("Unassigned"); user-editable'), line 102 ('room_number is user-settable any time (a room picker; None = Unassigned)') and line 115-116 (set_saved_zone_room, 'null = Unassigned'). The doc states the user override as a first-class, persistent choice; it never says a later read may reverse it.
survived.brands_affected: Eufy only — zone_membership returns room_number=None on Roborock (no per-pixel raster), so the `membership.get('room_number') is not None` arm never fires there.

survived.title: _generate_saved_zone_id / _generate_custom_layout_id guarantee uniqueness only against LIVE ids, so an id is reused after a delete — and saved-zone ids are durably referenced by queue steps and run profiles
survived.what_code_does: Both generators build `base = f'sz_|cl_{datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")}'` and only append `_2`, `_3`… while the candidate collides with a member of `existing`, which _create_saved_zone (line 1404) supplies as `set(zones)` — the CURRENTLY-LIVE ids of that map's saved_zones. A deleted id is not in that set, so the very next create in the same wall-clock second re-mints it. The docstrings assert these are 'Stable unique id' with a guard so 'rapid creates (and tests) never clash' — true for concurrent live ids, false across a delete. This matters because zone ids OUTLIVE the zone: core/manager.py:1736 stores `{'type': 'zone', 'zone_ids': [...]}` inside the map bucket's durable queue_breaks (and run-profile steps), and _handle_delete_saved_zone (line 2539-2554) pops the zone without sweeping a single one of those references. Resolution is by id at dispatch time (manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects, line 1855-1878), which 'silently skips' ids it cannot find.
survived.reproduction: (1) Queue step exists: `{'after_index': 2, 'step': {'type': 'zone', 'zone_ids': ['sz_20260731T142530']}}` for the zone 'Litter corner'. (2) User deletes 'Litter corner' — the queue step keeps the dead id and now silently resolves to nothing. (3) Within the same second (scripted delete+create, a double-tap flow, or a card that deletes-and-redraws) the user creates 'Under the couch'. _generate_saved_zone_id computes base='sz_20260731T142530', finds it absent from the live set, and returns it unchanged. (4) The next run reaches the queue step, _resolve_saved_zone_rects resolves 'sz_20260731T142530' to the NEW zone's bbox and dispatch_zone_clean fires it. The vacuum zone-cleans 'Under the couch' where the step said 'Litter corner'. The clock source widens this beyond one second in one case: datetime.now() is naive LOCAL time, so a DST fall-back replays a whole hour of id space.
survived.user_impact: Wrong physical area cleaned by a saved queue step or run profile, with no warning — the failure class is the most serious in this subsystem, but the window is narrow (delete and create must land in the same wall-clock second). The far more common outcome of the same missing-reference-sweep is benign: the step silently cleans nothing. Layout ids reuse the same way but nothing durable outside the bucket keys off them (the migrated layout's backdrop variant is the literal 'custom', and per-layout variants are re-derived on upload), so the layout side is latent.
survived.guards_checked: The same-second collision loop at lines 1371-1373 / 1382-1385 — only tests membership of the live `existing` set; _create_saved_zone's `set(zones)` (line 1404) — the live map's zones only, so per-map and point-in-time; _handle_delete_saved_zone (line 2539) — no reference sweep of queue_breaks or profile steps; manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects (core/manager.py:1866-1878) — validates that the id RESOLVES and that the geometry has >=3 points, but has no way to know the id was recycled; dispatch_zone_clean's brand count/size caps — orthogonal; no uuid, no monotonic counter, no tombstone of retired ids anywhere.
survived.doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'CustomLayout' ('layout_id is generated as "cl_{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS}" (with a same-second collision guard)') and docs/dev/07-queue-engine.md:575-576 (zone steps resolved at materialization via manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects over the map's saved_zones geometry). The docs describe the same-second guard as the whole uniqueness story and never state that ids must be unique over TIME, which the durable zone_ids references silently require.
survived.brands_affected: Both — saved zones and queue zone steps exist for Eufy and Roborock alike.

survived.title: adjust_map_segment persists a map-level record keyed by a segment id that CV re-analysis recycles — a nudge authored for one room silently re-attaches to whichever segment inherits that id
survived.what_code_does: Line 1752 stores the accumulated transform in `map_bucket['image_segment_adjustments'][segment_id]`, a map-level dict keyed purely by segment_id, with no fingerprint of the geometry it was authored against (no analyzed_at, no polygon hash, no bbox). CV segment ids are positional: adapters/eufy/segmentor.py:1289 mints `f'segment_{segment_id}'` from a running counter over detected components. _handle_analyze_map_image (line 1174) replaces `map_bucket['image_segments']` wholesale on force_reanalyze and never clears or invalidates image_segment_adjustments, and _handle_get_map_segments (line 1205-1208) blindly re-applies the old records to the new segments by id.
survived.reproduction: (1) User nudges 'segment_3' (the den) by delta_x=+40, delta_y=-25 to line its outline up with the backdrop; the record persists at image_segment_adjustments['segment_3']. (2) The robot re-explores and the user re-uploads the map image and taps Re-analyze (force_reanalyze=true). The segmenter now detects one extra component early in the scan, so the den is emitted as 'segment_4' and the hallway becomes 'segment_3'. (3) The next get_map_segments applies the stale record to the hallway: _apply_segment_adjustments shifts the hallway polygon by (+40, -25), rewrites its bbox and center_pixel, and tags it 'translated_manual' — while the den, which actually needed the nudge, renders unadjusted.
survived.user_impact: A displayed room outline is silently offset from its true position and falsely labelled as manually adjusted, and the correction the user made is lost from the room it belonged to. Display/linking only — segment polygons are not the dispatch geometry (room cleans go by room id, zone cleans by saved-zone geometry), so nothing physical goes wrong. Only bites installs that both use segment nudges and re-analyze after the map changed; a re-analyze that reproduces the same component order is harmless.
survived.guards_checked: The segment-existence check at line 1749-1750 — validates only at WRITE time and only against the current image_segments, so it cannot protect a record that outlives the segmentation it was written for; the zero-netting cleanup at line 1783-1794 — removes an entry only when the user manually nudges it back to zero; _handle_analyze_map_image (line 1174) — replaces image_segments and calls async_save with no adjustment invalidation; _apply_segment_adjustments (line 756-825) — matches purely on `str(seg.get('segment_id'))` with no cross-check that the polygon is the one the transform was authored against.
survived.doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'AdjustmentRecord' ('CV-segment edits only — written by adjust_map_segment, applied to image_segments at read time', 'Deltas accumulate across calls') and docs/dev/03-data-model.md §image_segments ('Re-running CV re-segments and forces a relink (accepted)'). The doc explicitly accepts that re-analysis breaks segment_room_LINKS, but says nothing about adjustments — and links break VISIBLY (the room shows unlinked) whereas an adjustment re-attaches INVISIBLY to a different shape. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §467 documents a different, adjacent caveat (cross-scope id collision) and is not this.
survived.brands_affected: Eufy only in practice — image_segment_adjustments is written against the CV image_segments store, which only the Eufy CV segmentor populates.

survived.title: map_id is documented as optional + auto-resolving on 6 presentation services but is vol.Required; a literal blank map_id silently mints and writes a phantom map bucket
survived.what_code_does: Every write handler in this block reads `map_id: str = call.data["map_id"]` (2108, 2150, 2195, 1943, 2010, 2053) and hands it straight to `ensure_map_bucket()`. Their schemas declare `vol.Required("map_id"): cv.string`. So a raster with no room pixels at all is wrapped as `{present: True, ...}` with no `reason`, and `roborock_render_data_from_candidates` (map_source_runtime.py:411, `if rd is not None: return rd`) stops scanning further candidate roots because it got a non-None answer.

Executed against the shipped module: `decode_roborock_v1_segments(blob)` returns room_ids=[] with 0 non-zero pixels (resolve_rid(0x07)==0), and `roborock_render_data(dec, {16: 'Kitchen'})` returns `present=True, width=200, height=150, room_names={'16': 'Kitchen'}`. Nothing surfaces a reason — the card, and diagnostics' self_check 'map decoded' verdict, both read this as a successfully decoded map. survived.title: raster_room_bboxes runs an O(width*height) pure-Python per-pixel loop directly on the Home Assistant event loop
survived.what_code_does: `for i, rid in enumerate(rp)` at line 200 iterates EVERY pixel of the decoded raster in Python, doing `i % w`, `i // w`, a dict `.get`, and up to four comparisons per pixel. There is no size cap: decode_roborock_v1_segments bounds width/height only by the blob length (lines 111-114), so the loop length is whatever the device's IMAGE block is. The call chain is entirely synchronous: raster_room_bboxes ← geometry_drift (line 259) ← map_source_runtime.roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates:434 ← diagnostics.py:503, which sits inside `_vacuum_diagnostics(...)` — a plain sync function invoked from the coroutine `async_get_config_entry_diagnostics` at diagnostics.py:571, in a list comprehension, once per vacuum, with no `async_add_executor_job`.
survived.reproduction: Roborock S6, map_state_source.backend == 'memory', a decodable raw blob. Settings → Devices & Services → Vacuum Agent → ⋮ → Download diagnostics. For an IMAGE block of 700x700 (a routine crop for a whole-floor S6 map) that is 490,000 Python loop iterations with two integer divisions and a dict lookup each, executed on the event loop thread. Contrast the render path for the SAME raster: decode_roborock_v1_segments + roborock_render_data touch every pixel only through `bytes.translate`, `set()`, `base64.b64encode` and `hashlib.sha1` — all C-level. The drift path is the only per-pixel Python loop in the module, and it is the one that is not offloaded.
survived.user_impact: Downloading diagnostics stalls the entire HA event loop — every integration, every automation trigger, the frontend websocket — for the duration of the scan. On x86 that is roughly 0.1-0.3 s for a mid-size map; on a Pi-class or NAS host with a large map it is comfortably into multiple seconds, long enough for HA's own loop-lag warnings and for a websocket-connected card to visibly freeze. It repeats once per configured Roborock vacuum in the same download. Not data loss, and only on a user-initiated diagnostics download — but it is the one path in this module with no cost bound at all.
survived.guards_checked: diagnostics.py:496-505 — a bare try/except around the call, no executor hop, no size or timeout guard. diagnostics.py:533-574 — `async_get_config_entry_diagnostics` is a coroutine and calls `_vacuum_diagnostics` synchronously at :571. map_source_coordinator.py:620 comments 'In-memory + pure -> loop-safe' — that claim covers the RENDER path (roborock_render_data_from_candidates), which is genuinely C-level; it does not cover the drift path, and the drift path has no equivalent claim or guard. decode_roborock_v1_segments has no maximum-dimension check that would bound the loop. geometry_drift/raster_room_bboxes have no early-exit or sampling.

survived.title: ro_dx/ro_dy are hardcoded 0 and the decoded top/left are discarded — the payload cannot express any offset between the raw IMAGE-block frame and the parser's rendered frame
survived.what_code_does: decode_roborock_v1_segments reads `top` and `left` from the IMAGE-block header (lines 97-98) and returns them (lines 122-123), and then no consumer in the module ever uses them: roborock_render_data ignores them and instead hardcodes `ro_dx: 0, ro_dy: 0` (lines 171-172) with `ro_width/ro_height` set equal to the canvas (lines 169-170), defended by the comment 'the raster IS the canvas (no outline frame)'. That comment is a CLAIM that the raw IMAGE-block frame is pixel-identical to the frame every other Roborock overlay is normalized to — namely map_source_runtime._mapdata_projector (:438-470), which normalizes by the PARSER's rendered `image.data.size` after `dims.to_img` has applied the parser's trim/scale. The ro_dx/ro_dy fields exist precisely to carry such an offset (Eufy fills them from _outline_geometry, map_source.py:662-663); Roborock is the sibling where the knob is present but pinned to 0.
survived.reproduction: Conditional on the HA roborock integration's ImageConfig trim, which is not inspectable from this repo. If the parser trims T rows off the rendered image's bottom of an H-row block: raw row r normalizes to (H-1-r)/H in this module's frame (raster_room_bboxes:219) but to (H-T-1-r)/(H-T) in the parser frame. H=700, T=50, r=100 → 0.8557 vs 0.8446, a 0.011 normalized delta = 0.39 m on a 700 px x 50 mm/px (35 m) map. If T==0 the frames coincide and this is inert. The shipped geometry_drift diagnostic is exactly the instrument that settles it: one 'Download diagnostics' on the real S6 reports `aligned` (frames coincide, no defect) or a systematic `max_center_delta` (frames differ, defect live).
survived.user_impact: IF the frames differ: the card draws the raster full-bleed at 0..1 while every overlay it composites on top — room bboxes, robot/dock anchors, no-go and no-mop quads, saved zones — comes from map_state_source in the parser frame, so overlays sit offset from the rooms they label; `roomIdAtContentPct` (src/state/map.js:931-966) names the wrong room for clicks near a boundary; and a zone drawn on the raster is converted to device mm through `correspondences_from_mapdata` (the PARSER frame) at dispatch/manager.py:154, so app_zoned_clean cleans a displaced rectangle — the robot physically cleans the wrong strip of floor. survived.title: The IMAGE-block dimension guard is `header_len >= 16`, but the four dims occupy the LAST 16 bytes of a header whose first 8 are the fixed type/len fields — anything under 24 reads dims out of the header's own metadata
survived.what_code_does: Line 96 gates the dim reads on `header_len >= 16`, then reads top/left/height/width at `pos + header_len - 16 .. -4` (lines 97-100). The block header's first 8 bytes are fixed: type (int16 @0x00), header_len (int16 @0x02), data_len (int32 @0x04). So the four dim int32s only occupy bytes the format actually reserves for them when `header_len >= 24` — which is what the real v1 layout uses (tests/unit/test_roborock_raw_map.py:45-55 builds exactly a 24-byte header with dims at offsets 8/12/16/20 == header_len-16/-12/-8/-4). For header_len in 16..23 the guard passes and the reads slide backwards over the type/header_len/data_len fields.
survived.reproduction: A block with type=2, header_len=20, data_len=D: `top = _u32(raw, pos+4)` == D (the data_len field re-read as a coordinate), `left = _u32(raw, pos+8)`, `height = _u32(raw, pos+12)`, `width = _u32(raw, pos+16)`. With header_len=16: `top = _u32(raw, pos+0)` == type | (header_len << 16) == 2 | 0x100000. The values are then carried into `image` (line 101) and, if `width*height <= data_len` and `data_start + width*height <= n` happen to hold, into a returned raster with garbage dims — no further sanity check exists.
survived.user_impact: Not reachable on a well-formed v1 blob (roborock uses >= 24-byte IMAGE headers). It matters as the module's stated defence posture: the docstring at lines 14-16 says the byte walk is 'mirrored from vacuum-map-parser-roborock ... so a firmware format change is a one-file fix', and a firmware/format change is precisely the event that would present a short header. A `>= 24` guard would reject it as unparseable (returning None, which the caller degrades cleanly); `>= 16` accepts it and can emit a plausible-shaped raster built on coordinates read out of the header's own length fields. The other unchecked-offset risks in this walk are genuinely covered (see clean_areas) — this is the one gate that is looser than the format it guards.
survived.guards_checked: decode_roborock_v1_segments:91 `header_len < 8 or pos + header_len > n` — bounds the read but says nothing about whether 16 bytes of DIMS fit after the 8 bytes of fixed fields. There is no minimum/maximum plausible-dimension check anywhere in the module.
survived.doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §map_render 'v1 only' spells out the layout: 'IMAGE block type == 2; top/left/height/width = int32 @ header[header_len-16..-4]' and the module docstring lines 18-25 repeat it — both describe the offsets relative to header_len without stating the minimum header_len that makes them valid, which is how the off-by-8 guard slipped in.

The finder performed a LEXICAL normalization (as os.path.normpath does) that neither os.path.join nor open() performs. I executed the exact reproduction and the write failed. The finding's own sentence "open(...,"wb") succeeds because the directory already exists" is the false premise. (Its arithmetic is separately off by one: normpath of that path lands in <config>/eufy_vacuum/www, not <config>/www.) The residual true observation — that a map_id containing "/" raises an uncaught FileNotFoundError out of _write_and_measure instead of the structured {"saved": false, "reason": ...} shape — is real but is already reported as part of A3-IMAGE--5 and does not support this finding's title, severity, or security framing.

There is no IndexError path; the `except (IndexError, ValueError)` at line 130 is belt-and-braces, not load-bearing.

Forward-progress / advance arithmetic (lines 102-106) — verified the docstring's claim rather than trusting it: `step = data_len + raw[pos+0x02]` equals `data_len + header_len` for every header_len < 256, because header_len = raw[pos+2] | raw[pos+3]<<8 and a value under 256 forces raw[pos+3] == 0, making the low byte the whole value. `pos += step` therefore lands exactly on `data_start + data_len`, the next block. `step == 0` is reachable only when data_len == 0 AND raw[pos+2] == 0, i.e. header_len is a multiple of 256 — and that case breaks. No infinite-loop path exists.

Truncated / absent / non-bytes blob handling (lines 79-114) — a truncated IMAGE block is correctly REJECTED, which was the headline hunt: the header can survive intact while the payload is cut, and `data_start + pixel_count > n` (line 113) catches exactly that. `pixel_count > data_len` (line 111) rejects a header claiming more pixels than the block declares. `n < 4` returns None. A non-bytes input raises TypeError/ValueError inside `bytes(raw)` and returns None; the one input that slips past that — an int, where `bytes(5)` yields five zero bytes rather than raising — still falls out as None via `header_len < 8`. None, b'', b'\x00', and random bytes all return None (confirmed by tests RRD-4 and by inspection).

`raster_room_bboxes` flip normalization (lines 218-221) — proven by arithmetic, not accepted. Raw rows [b1..b3] inclusive map to rendered rows [h-1-b3 .. h-1-b1], normalized to [(h-b3-1)/h, (h-b1)/h]; the code emits `1-(b3+1)/h` and `1-b1/h`, identical. The non-flip branch is the plain inclusive→exclusive conversion. This matches the reference parser's write order (raw row i → image row height-1-i) and is the exact inverse of the card's `pyN = (H-1) - ny*H` at src/state/map.js:953. Correct in both branches.

`_bbox_iou` (lines 225-236) — degenerate and non-overlapping boxes are handled: `max(0.0, ...)` clamps negative extents, `inter <= 0` short-circuits before any division, and `union > 0` guards the final divide. No ZeroDivisionError and no negative IoU is producible.

`geometry_drift` input coercion (lines 250-258) — hostile input from `rooms_from_mapdata` is handled without raising and without coercing to a wrong number: non-dict entries, a missing/None `number`, a non-list or wrong-length bbox, and non-numeric bbox values are each skipped via explicit isinstance/len/try-except rather than defaulted. `min_iou` correctly reports 0.0 rather than the optimistic pre-loop 1.0 when `common` is empty (line 285), and `aligned` correctly starts with `bool(common)` so an empty comparison can never read as aligned.
